reference_opening.argument: This video is scam content because the speaker promotes BitClub Ethereum mining-pool participation as passive income, claiming about 33 ETH and more than sixfold investment growth. The speaker pairs those claims with displayed pool and wallet records and says profitability will rise as ETH grows, while providing a BitClub URL and contact route.

citations.quote: I want to make a to do my passive income calculation for a mining pool of Ethereum
In total we get a little more than 32 ETH in fact 33 ETH
six times more than 6 times my investments have been multiplied
I want to tell you and wish you, probably, successful investment friends

opening.argument: The calculation is explicitly tied to changing market prices, not presented as a fixed payout: the speaker says the result depends on ETH's price and uses a prior price of $350 for a separate calculation. He also notes that ETH is low “today.” That makes the return estimate conditional on a volatile asset, rather than a promise that viewers will receive a particular amount. The video does not state that returns are guaranteed or that the calculation will hold for everyone.

citations.quote: even though EPHERES is low today
when I calculated the profitability, last time the price of ether was $ 350
the more the profitability of the pool will increase

rebuttal.rebuttal: The cited earnings and investment-growth figures describe the speaker's calculation, but they do not establish a guaranteed outcome for a viewer. The opening's own evidence shows a price-dependent comparison: it uses an earlier ETH price, while the speaker acknowledges that the price changes. A favorable example can be persuasive without proving a fixed or assured return.

citations.quote: when I calculated the profitability, last time the price of ether was $ 350
So, the more ETH grows,

true_side_reply.rebuttal: Price sensitivity does not remove the central return claim: the speaker says the pool produced about 33 ETH and that his investment multiplied more than six times, then tells viewers that profitability rises as ETH grows. Nothing here warns viewers that the calculation may not represent their results or that they could lose money.

citations.quote: In total we get a little more than 32 ETH in fact 33 ETH
six times more than 6 times my investments have been multiplied
the more the profitability of the pool will increase

opening.argument: The video is organized around a worked calculation and a website walkthrough: the speaker says he will calculate passive income, then moves through pool and wallet information and compares the resulting ETH with exchange prices. The displayed account history and wallet interface make the subject an operational demonstration of how he arrives at his figures, not merely an unsupported claim. The material supports classifying its central activity as showing and calculating account data; it does not establish that the figures were independently verified or that a viewer is promised the same result.

citations.quote: I want to make a to do my passive income calculation for a mining pool of Ethereum
Now let's go to the Ethereum wallet

rebuttal.rebuttal: The prosecution reads the calculation as a pitch, but the specific material is a walkthrough of the speaker's own pool and wallet figures. Showing an account interface does not prove a viewer can reproduce the outcome, and a calculation based on market prices is not itself evidence of a guaranteed return. The link and closing investment wish do not establish what happens after a viewer follows the link.

citations.quote: Now let's go to the Ethereum wallet
when I calculated the profitability, last time the price of ether was $ 350
I want to tell you and wish you, probably, successful investment friends

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The walkthrough is not neutral instruction alone. The speaker calls the calculation passive income, presents his pool earnings as more than 32 ETH, compares them with investment growth, and closes by wishing viewers successful investment. Those choices turn the demonstration into an investment promotion even if the displayed records do not independently verify payouts.

citations.quote: I want to make a to do my passive income calculation for a mining pool of Ethereum
In total we get a little more than 32 ETH in fact 33 ETH
I want to tell you and wish you, probably, successful investment friends

opening.argument: What is shown is a mining-pool share purchase history and account interface, followed by a calculation of ETH and its market value. That supports an ordinary service-and-account presentation, not proof of a broader fraud mechanism. The supplied material does not show a viewer making a deposit, being asked for credentials, receiving a guaranteed return, or earning through a downline. A pool purchase and an optimistic personal calculation may warrant scrutiny, but those facts alone do not establish that the service is fraudulent.

citations.quote: Now let's go to the Ethereum wallet
Let's look at the current EPHEUR rate

rebuttal.rebuttal: The prosecution's figures show what the speaker claims about his own pool account, not that the service guarantees equivalent returns to others. The URL and contact route establish that viewers can find more information, but the supplied evidence does not show what the linked destination offers or what a viewer would be asked to do. Do not infer an unshown deposit or credential request from the presence of a link.

citations.quote: In total we get a little more than 32 ETH in fact 33 ETH
I will answer all questions on VK

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The case is not based only on a link or an unshown credential request. The speaker connects a paid pool-share history to a passive-income calculation, claims about 33 ETH and more than sixfold growth, then invites investment-minded viewers to follow up. Those claims make the promotion itself relevant even without proof that a viewer deposited money or that a downline exists.
